# Eval Run Protocol

## Isolation

Baseline ("without_skill") arms must be unable to read the skill. In iterations 1 and 2 they
could: the fixtures sit next to the skill on disk, fixture guide files carry a
"GENERATED by rebuild-kit render_guide.py" breadcrumb, and baseline agents followed it to
`rebuild-kit/scripts/render_guide.py` and read the real implementation. A grader proved the
contamination with a byte-for-byte re-render match, which is why eval-1's 8/8-vs-8/8 tie means
nothing.

The first attempt at a fix was to physically move the skill directory out of the repo while the
baseline ran, and move it back afterward. Do not do this. It leaves the developer's tree
mutilated if anything crashes before the restore (it did), it makes the two arms impossible to
run concurrently, and it closes only one of the four ways skill content is reachable.

Isolation is now kernel-enforced by `isolation/run_arm.py`, which runs the executor under a
macOS seatbelt profile. Nothing is moved, nothing needs cleaning up, arms run concurrently, and
a crash cannot leave the repo in a bad state. The baseline profile denies reads of:

| Vector | Why it leaks |
|---|---|
| the whole repo root | the skill implementation itself |
| — same rule | `evals.json`, which contains the grading assertions verbatim |
| — same rule | prior iterations' `with_skill/outputs/`, which contain copies of skill scripts |
| — same rule | `.git`, which serves the full skill from history even if the worktree is hidden |
| `~/.claude/projects` | transcripts and memory from earlier with-skill sessions quote the skill |

The `with_skill` profile is identical except it re-allows the skill subtree — so that arm still
cannot read the assertions or prior outputs, which the old protocol never protected either.

The one vector a filesystem sandbox cannot close is the network: the skill is a pushed GitHub
remote. `isolation/guard_hook.py` denies tool calls that look like remote retrieval of it, and
logs every tool call to `audit.jsonl` regardless.

## After cloning (required once)

```sh
cd evals && python3 git_bundles.py unpack fixtures
```

The fixtures are git repos, and git cannot commit a nested repo's history, so a fresh clone gets
fixture trees with no `.git`. That does not fail loudly: git walks up to the outer repo, and
`rev-parse HEAD` in `fixtures/ticketd` returns this repository's latest commit instead. Evals 0
and 1 assert that `rebuild.json`'s `legacy_ref` matches the fixture's own HEAD, so without this
step they compare against the wrong SHA and fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the
skill. (This is the same walk-up that `scaffold.py`'s `pin_legacy()` had to be fixed for.)

The bundles are committed, so this restores the real history. It is a no-op if the fixtures
already have their `.git`.

## Running

```sh
cd evals/isolation
python3 verify_isolation.py             # required before every iteration; free, no model calls
python3 verify_isolation.py --live      # adds a real agent ordered to go find the skill

python3 run_arm.py --eval 0 --config without_skill --iteration iteration-3 --model sonnet
python3 run_arm.py --eval 0 --config with_skill    --iteration iteration-3 --model sonnet
```

`verify_isolation.py` executes real read attempts against each vector in the table and asserts
the kernel refuses them, then asserts the with-skill arm can still read the skill and unrelated
work still functions. If it reports `ISOLATION BROKEN`, the run is not worth doing.

`run_arm.py` stages the fixture into a neutrally-named `/private/tmp` directory (nothing in the
path names the skill), runs the executor there, then copies results into
`iteration-N/eval-<id>-<name>/<config>/`:

- `outputs/` — the agent's work, for `grade_checks.py`
- `final_report.md` — the agent's closing report
- `transcript.jsonl` — full stream, replacing hand-inspection of the session
- `audit.jsonl` + `isolation.json` — every tool call, the profile actually used, and a
  `review_recommended` flag
- `timing.json` — duration, tokens, cost, turns, captured automatically

Timing no longer has to be copied out of a completion notification by hand.

## Grading for contamination

Read `isolation.json`. `blocked_calls > 0` means the agent tried to fetch the skill remotely.
`skill_probe_calls > 0` means it went hunting locally — the reads were denied, so this is not
contamination by itself, but the run deserves a look. `review_recommended` is true if either
fired.

## Archiving a finished iteration

Eval outputs contain whole git repos — the rewrite roots the agent generated, plus copies of the
legacy fixture. Git cannot commit a nested repo's files: it records the directory as a gitlink
and the files never enter the archive (for iteration-2 that was 2,837 files on disk versus 163
actually committable). Adding files individually does not help; git refuses to cross a nested
repo boundary.

Deleting the history instead would be lossy, because `grade_checks.py` verifies the pinned
`legacy_ref` by running `git rev-parse HEAD` against it. So pack the history into bundles before
committing:

```sh
python3 git_bundles.py pack   iteration-3     # before `git add`
python3 git_bundles.py unpack iteration-3     # before re-grading an archived run
```

`pack` clones each bundle back and compares HEAD before it removes any `.git`, and records each
repo's HEAD sha and branch in `_git_bundles/manifest.json` so `unpack` restores the exact state
rather than guessing a branch. Round trip on iteration-2: 15/15 HEADs identical, worktrees clean,
17MB down to 5.1MB.

Note that legacy trees are checked out read-only by the skill's own protection mechanism, so
`rm -rf` on a copied iteration dir needs `chmod -R u+w` first.

## Caveats

Requires macOS with `sandbox-exec`. On any other host `run_arm.py` refuses to run rather than
produce a result that looks clean but isn't.

The guard hook must be staged outside the repo before use — the baseline profile denies the repo,
so a hook referenced at its repo path silently never fires, taking the audit log and the network
block with it. `install_guard()` handles this; `verify_isolation.py --live` asserts the log is
non-empty so the failure cannot return unnoticed.

## Contaminated results

Keep contaminated run dirs for the record but move them out of the iteration directory's
`eval-*` glob (e.g. `iteration-N/_contaminated/`) so the benchmark aggregator excludes them.
Iterations 1 and 2 predate enforced isolation; their eval-1 baselines are known-contaminated and
their other baselines are unverified.
